title: Lesson 2: Salvation and Baptism
description: Salvation is new life that God gives and you receive by faith. Baptism is the first visible sign of that life. This lesson walks the Romans Road, explains what baptism means, and shows why you can be sure you belong to God.

blocks.text: In the last lesson you looked back over your story and saw God's hand in it. Now you will look at the most important moment in that story: when God gave you new life in Jesus.

blocks.title: The Greenhouse
blocks.text:
Picture the image for this course: a young plant with young roots in a pot inside a greenhouse. The plant cannot make itself grow. A gardener can water it, adjust the light, and protect it from the cold, but the life inside that seed comes from God. The Bible says it is God who gives the growth (1 Corinthians 3:6).

Here is something easy to miss. For a while, all of that life is underground. The seed has split open and roots are reaching down, but nobody can see it yet. Then one morning a green shoot breaks through the soil, and everyone can see what was already true.

That is a picture of this lesson. Salvation is God giving you a new life you could never produce yourself. Baptism is the first green shoot, the moment the life God started on the inside shows up where everyone can see it.

You cannot force spiritual growth any more than you can force a seed to sprout. What you can do is tend the environment: read the Bible, learn to pray, join a Christian community, and stay close to Jesus. Welcome to this discipleship greenhouse, where you faithfully show up and trust God with the growth.
Salvation

Salvation is the word the Bible uses to describe what God did for you through Jesus. Simply put, we were separated from God because of sin, and Jesus came to rescue us, bring us back to God, and give us a life that lasts forever. It is not something you earned. It is something God offered freely, and you received it by putting your faith in Jesus Christ as your Lord and Savior. Salvation is not just a moment, it is the beginning of a whole new life. God saved you, He is growing you, and He will be faithful to finish what He started in you.

For God so loved the world, that he gave his only Son, that whoever believes in him should not perish but have eternal life. For God did not send his Son into the world to condemn the world, but in order that the world might be saved through him.

blocks.text: How can someone be saved and become a Christian?

Paul's letter to the Romans explains the gospel so clearly that people call the path through it "The Romans Road." You can remember it with three letters, the ABCs of salvation: Admit, Believe, and Confess. Walk through each stop below.

Notice who does the work on that road. You admit, believe, and confess, but none of those steps earn anything. They are empty hands receiving a gift that Jesus already paid for. Salvation is God's gift of new life, received by faith.

blocks.text: Baptism

Baptism is a visible symbol of what God has already done inside of you. It is the outward sign that you belong to the people of God, that you have repented and put your faith in Jesus Christ. Baptism does not save you, but it is an act of obedience for every believer in response to the words of Jesus. In Matthew 28:19, Jesus told His followers to go and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit. When you are baptized, you are being baptized into the family of God because of the finished work of Jesus Christ.

When a believer steps into the water, they are declaring that their old self has passed away and they are embracing their new identity in Christ. Going under the water pictures the washing away of sin and the death of the old life. Rising up out of the water pictures the beauty of resurrection, that you are a new creation in Jesus. Galatians 2:20 says, "I have been crucified with Christ. It is no longer I who live, but Christ who lives in me." Baptism is a sign and a celebration that you belong to God, that you have been cleansed by the work of Jesus, and that you are now sent to be a blessing to others.

Do you not know that all of us who have been baptized into Christ Jesus were baptized into his death? We were buried therefore with him by baptism into death, in order that, just as Christ was raised from the dead by the glory of the Father, we too might walk in newness of life.

If you have trusted Jesus and have not been baptized yet, you do not need to wait until you feel more grown up in your faith. The green shoot comes early in a plant's life, not late. Tell a pastor or the person walking through this study with you that you want to take that step.
2.4 - Where are you with baptism right now: already baptized, ready to take the step, or still unsure?
You Are a New Creation
When you become a Christian by putting your faith in Jesus as Lord and Savior, you are a new creation. You have been adopted by the Father into the family of God.

Therefore, if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation. The old has passed away; behold, the new has come... For our sake he made him to be sin who knew no sin, so that in him we might become the righteousness of God.

Some days you will not feel new. You will still sin, and you may wonder whether anything really changed. Your salvation does not rest on how you feel on a given day. It rests on what Jesus has done, and God wants you to be sure of it.
I write these things to you who believe in the name of the Son of God, that you may know that you have eternal life.
2.5 - Which part of 2 Corinthians 5:17, 21 encourages you most today?
Lesson 2 Review

Salvation is God's gift of new life, received by faith in Jesus and never earned. The Romans Road shows the way: admit your sin, believe in Jesus, and confess Him as Lord. Baptism is the first green shoot, the outward sign of the life God has already started inside you. And because your salvation rests on Jesus and not on you, you can know that you have eternal life.
In the next lesson, you will learn to talk with the God who saved you, using the pattern Jesus gave His disciples for prayer.

blocks.heading: Introduction to John 4, 5, and 6
blocks.intro: In John 4-6, Jesus reveals Himself as the source of living water, the bread of life, and the one with power over sickness, storms, and death. Watch for the way He meets people right where they are and offers them something they did not know they needed.
